# Chang Chung-yuan — *Tao: A New Way of Thinking* (2014)

[Source index](../../../README.md) · [Reading entrance](../../../../../../README.md) · [48 movements](../../../../../../section-rooms/README.md)

## Bibliographic identity

The work is Chang Chung-yuan's translation of the Tao Tê Ching with an introduction and chapter-by-chapter commentaries. Chang (1907–1988), Professor of Philosophy at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and author of *Creativity and Taoism*, reads each chapter beside Western metaphysics — Heidegger above all, with Hegel, Schopenhauer, Jung, Plato, Kant, and Nietzsche named by the publisher; the chapters Frank read also quote Nishida.

The selected edition is the Singing Dragon reprint, published 21 January 2014, 240 pages, ISBN 978-1-84819-201-0. Singing Dragon is an imprint of Jessica Kingsley Publishers (London and Philadelphia); the publisher's product record verifies title, subtitle, format, extent, date, and ISBN. The work was first published in 1975 by Harper & Row (New York). Title renderings vary across records — the publisher prints "Tao – A New Way of Thinking" over the subtitle "A Translation of the Tao Tê Ching with an Introduction and Commentaries," while library records give "Tao, a new way of thinking" — and the Chicago forms below join the double subtitle in the standard way.

Frank's complete encounter notes cite pp. 83–143, moving through selected commentaries within chapters 20–42. Their first sequence, pp. 83–93 and chapters 20–22, continues through identity and belonging, the p.99 mirror-first vocation, the thing and fourfold, motion and opposites, the twofold One, and the p.143 emergence of multiplicity. These are the notes' own locators. They are presumed to track the 2014 pagination of the copy at hand; collating them against the physical copy is the open verification step, and if the copy proves to be the 1975 printing the house's selected edition should be re-decided rather than silently repaginated.

The sibling `NOTES.md` is Frank G. Taylor's authorial encounter with the work. Its authorial developments retain their own attribution, and its copied passages are leads until verified against the selected edition.

## Source scholarship

Chang's operation is that of a philosopher-translator: he renders the Tao Tê Ching so that its ontology can be heard within Western metaphysics, and his commentaries stage direct meetings — Heidegger's claim that the Nothing is more original than the Not and negation, the region as the open cleared by the primal conflict of opposites, and the passage in *On the Way to Language* where Heidegger ventures that Tao could be the way that gives all ways; Jung on the identity of opposites from *Psychological Types* and on the unconscious as worldly and objective in scope; Nishida on the union of subject and object as the point where religion and morality are exhausted. Chapter 20's commentary distinguishes the self-identity of contradictions as lived in actual life from any unification of opposites achieved through intellection; chapter 21's turns on Tao as indistinct and ineffable yet containing all forms, the creativity that is the source of all things.

Frank's encounter-intent, recovered from `NOTES.md` and named here as his and only his: he maps the lived self-identity of contradictions to `0/1` and the intellectual synthesis to `4+2`, with the MEF lenses giving the synthesis its real meta-epistemic standing; he adds the dia-ballein failure mode — one-sided calculative thought as the misapprehension of the original identity of opposites — as the project's own extension, flagged as such in the notes and carrying the mythic register of the fall deliberately; he hears Heidegger's priority of the Nothing as the exact shape of Zero's priority to the `(−1)` of cancellation; he reads Tao's indistinctness-containing-all-forms as Mono/Poly, the `0/1` and `1/0`; he takes Heidegger's Tao passage as a pointer to Epi-Logos, logos returning to the Saying prior to the said; and he links Chang's creativity to Whitehead's, with QL as the archetypal form of concrescence and the `0/1`–`1/0` pair as Spanda. His note registers the encounter's force: he finds the whole `(0/1)/(1/0)` self-identity effort to be about Tao.

Claim boundary: Chang translates and comments; he formulates neither QL, nor the dia-ballein/sym-ballein pair, nor the Spanda equations. The evidential relation for each mapping is Argued from or Resonant with, to be fixed passage by passage at verification. Chang's commentary deepens and tests the two-logics fulcrum and the Zero thread; it does not derive them.

Nested-quotation warning: the passages Frank copied include Chang quoting Nishida, Jung (*Psychological Types*), and Heidegger (*Existence and Being*; *On the Way to Language*). Until each is collated in its own primary edition, any such wording is double transmission through Chang and may be attributed only as "quoted by Chang," on the same pattern as the Watson–Gans chain in `watson-1998-resonance-of-emptiness`.

## Passages and excerpts

No passage cards yet. `NOTES.md` carries quotation leads at pp. 83–143 (2014 pagination presumed). The complete inventory retains two connected sequences:

- **pp. 83–93:** the Nishida passages on true self and subject–object union (p. 83); chapter 20's self-identity of contradictions (p. 84); Jung's *Psychological Types* and unconscious passages (pp. 85–86); the region (p. 87); the Heidegger Nothing passages and Chang's Tao comparison (p. 89); the *On the Way to Language* Tao passage (p. 90); indistinct form and liberation from delusion (pp. 90–91); chapter 22 on identifying opposites as one (p. 92); and motion–quiescence with Hegel/Nishida comparisons (p. 93).
- **pp. 95–143:** identity as belonging (p. 95); selflessness and thought's limit; the chapter24 pride passage (p. 97); chapter25's greatness of humanity (p. 99), beside which Frank develops AI as the mirror that turns toward thought's limit first; the four greatnesses and *wu* (pp. 100–101); the thing as gathering and the fourfold's nearness/farness (pp. 101–102); art, poetry and disclosed spirit, followed by Kumarajiva and the thing (p. 103); positive/negative and differentiation (p. 109); Jung on living polarity and the *Secret of the Golden Flower* (p. 110); freedom from opposites and releasement; chapters30–31 on war and its accounting; chapter32's names and unity, followed by the source-fidelity note explicitly marked p.120; chapter33's middle way (p. 121); region/circle and the great image (pp. 124–125); chapter36's mutual acting (p. 127); chapter39's twofold One (pp. 134–135); and chapter42's emergence of multiplicity, followed by Nishida's universal (p. 143).

The notes articulate these passages through QL, Spanda, Mono/Poly, the two logics, Epi-Logos, model orchestration and the mirror's vocation. Those developments disclose Frank's intent. Each copied source lead remains `unverified` until transcribed and collated against the selected edition; nested Nishida, Jung, Heidegger, Hegel, Kumarajiva and other attributed wording additionally needs its own transmission checked before attribution beyond Chang's commentary. No wording from `NOTES.md` may be printed as a verified external quotation.
